title: Recording for Norman Granz and Pablo
summary: He met Norman Granz in New York; recent albums include a trumpet date and sessions with Cleanhead, about three records a year.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Mmmmmmmnp. Back to you. Uh, your wife, Pat, made some notes here of important times that...things that have happened here. She mentioned...one of the things she has here is your recordings for Norman Granz on...on Pablo. When did you first meet Norman?
I met Norman years ago.
He used to run some sessions at Billy Berg's, didn't he?
Huh?
Didn't he used to run jam sessions at Billy Berg's...one of Billy Berg's clubs?
No.
No? Where did you meet him?
He...uh...I met him in...New York City. He always had the big bands...the big jazz shows...with Ella Fitzgerald...all them people...Count Basie...all them kinda people like that. He
Reel 5
has a jazz show now. I record for him now on...Freedom label.
You made that record with, uh, the trumpet players...uh, a couple of years ago, right?
Yeah.
With...uh, lessee...Dizzy, Roy Eldridge...uh, "Sweets" Edison and Clark Terry. Right?
Yeah, made it with all of 'em.
And then you took the same thing up an'...an' appeared at Monterey. Right?
Yeah, we went to Monterey.
Monterey Jazz Festival. And you've...you talked about recording with "Cleanhead" and Basie just recently.
Yeah.
And then you've got another album with "Cleanhead" on it, I know, because I have that album, and, uh, what else have you done for Norman?
Oh, I've recorded for him alla time.
How many records, about...how many records a year do you make for Norman Granz?
We only make about three a year.
